fixes.explanation: This one is true, friend. Mark 1:11 says a voice came from heaven: "You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased." The words "beloved Son" are right there. No need to second-guess this one.
I can see why a messenger sounds like a guard, but that's not what the text says. The words say this messenger goes ahead to "…prepare Your way." Guarding gates isn't anywhere in the verse.

Right on the money, baker. The voice is calling in the wilderness, "Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him." Those straight paths are right there in Mark 1:3. Mark is telling us the Lord is coming, and the way needs to be ready.

A tax would make for a short sermon, friend, with a long line of people leaving. Mark 1:4 says John is "…preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins." No tax and no walls are in that verse. Forgiveness is the message.

Yes, baker! Mark 1:5 says, "Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River." They confessed their sins, and they were baptized. So the statement that they don't confess is false.
That's the menu, friend. Mark 1:6 says, "His food was locusts and wild honey." Locusts are insects, and the honey is wild. I've burned some batches in my day, but even my worst one beats that.
Bread and fish is a fair guess, friend, but it isn't what the text says. Mark 1:6 says, "His food was locusts and wild honey." It's a wilderness menu, through and through.
Lamb and bitter herbs is a fair guess, friend, but it isn't on John's menu. Mark 1:6 says, "His food was locusts and wild honey." That's what he eats out in the wilderness.
Yes, friend. Mark 1:10 says Jesus "…saw the heavens breaking open and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove." The Spirit is what comes down, and it comes "like a dove." It's a gentle picture.
A pillar of fire shows up in Exodus 13:21, but not in this scene. In Mark 1:10, Jesus sees "…the Spirit descending on Him like a dove." It's a quiet image, nothing blazing.
Seven is a fair guess, but it isn't the number here. Mark 1:13 says, "…He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan." The number in this verse is forty.
